sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The ledgerlite tests pass with this command, run from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\c\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both tests pass: `test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`.

Without `PYTHONPATH=src` the run fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. The package sits under `src/` and isn't installed. The project has no `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py` or `conftest.py` to put it on the path. I didn't change any files.

I used the system Python 3.13 and didn't touch the `.recalith` venv.

In a native Windows shell the equivalent is `set PYTHONPATH=src && python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. In PowerShell it's `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. The full suite passes: 3 tests, including the new one.

The new test is `test_close_requires_zero_balance` in `tests/test_ledger.py`. It checks that closing an account with a non-zero balance raises and leaves the account in place. It then checks that the same account closes once its balance is back to zero.

Closing an account that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance()` does. You didn't specify that case, so say if you want a `ValueError` there instead.

I ran the suite with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, the `ledgerlite` import fails.
